sections.title: Architecture
sections.content: Evidence-gated artifact DAG separates lifecycle ownership from non-authorizing deterministic and Bootstrap evidence. Acceptance owns closure, route, imports, and final acceptance; Bootstrap owns isolated semantic execution and recovery only.

sections.title: Canonical Evidence
sections.content: Use a shared strict canonical-evidence primitive with domain-separated complete identity references, immutable artifacts, verify-only legacy support, and cross-consumer vectors. Reject ambiguous JSON, identity, path, range, scope, and stale-input conditions.

sections.title: Acceptance Route
sections.content: Admission requires a current implementation-complete handoff and immutable baseline/candidate. Acceptance builds changed-set and consumer closure, executes real required checks, then defaults to deterministic_only. Focused or full Bootstrap requires an explicit Acceptance-owned request record; failures and pauses are non-authorizing.

sections.title: Bootstrap Execution
sections.content: Explicit Bootstrap work uses stable segment descriptors, immutable segment-only snapshots, inherited access proof, three isolated review roles, and an independent verifier only for accepted P0/P1 findings. Receipts remain non-authorizing and require exact binding validation.

sections.title: Runtime Recovery
sections.content: Bootstrap runtime uses immutable policy-bound process events. Heartbeats refresh liveness only; validated effective progress controls no-progress windows. Lease occupancy is conjunctive, recovery is event-based, retries are bounded, and transport failures cannot become semantic completion.

sections.title: Delivery Plan
sections.content: Seven ordered slices cover canonical evidence and migration; runtime recovery; acceptance pipeline; projection and isolation; semantic import/finalization; and scale/parity rollout. Whole-directory behavior remains until rollout gates and semantic parity pass.

sections.title: Command Contract
sections.content: The registry defines fixed real RED/GREEN validation programs for canonical evidence, migration, runtime, acceptance pipeline, projection, import, rollout, and terminal validation. Receipts must bind executable, inputs, environment projection, results, and policy.

sections.title: Repair Findings
sections.content: Round 9 repairs three P1 gaps: remove inferred Bootstrap route upgrades, make deterministic check outcomes machine-verifiable, and require controlled Acceptance-owned admission for optional Bootstrap requests.

sections.title: Repair Scope
sections.content: Repair slices target S3 acceptance routing and evidence, S5 deterministic/default finalization and explicit Bootstrap import, and S6 regression proof of zero default-route Bootstrap calls and rejection of forged or inferred upgrades.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.content: Acceptance criteria require complete closure, real checks, deterministic default routing, explicit-request-only semantic review, isolated three-role coverage, bounded recovery, canonical identity safety, preserved historical failures, semantic parity, telemetry, and Acceptance-only lifecycle publication.
